title: An LPDDR-based CXL-PNM Platform for TCO-efficient Inference of Transformer-based Large Language Models
problem: GPUs have limited memory capacity requiring frequent model parameter transfers from CPU over slow interconnects like PCIe/NVLink, and multi-GPU systems suffer from frequent intermediate value transfers among devices creating a bandwidth bottleneck.
motivation: LLM inference is essential for commercial services but GPU-based systems are constrained by memory capacity and interconnect bandwidth limitations.
method: Instead of having computation far from memory and moving data across slow interconnects, the system places compute hardware directly adjacent to large memory banks, connected via Compute eXpress Link (CXL), a much faster interconnect than traditional GPU connections like PCIe. The memory uses LPDDR5X technology—the efficient type found in smartphones—and provides 512GB of capacity with 1.1TB/s of bandwidth. A CXL-PNM controller and LLM inference accelerator manage this configuration, and a Python-compatible software layer makes it work transparently with existing code.
key_novelty: Using cheap, efficient smartphone memory (LPDDR5X) connected directly to processing hardware via Compute eXpress Link (CXL) to eliminate the memory bottleneck that slows down large language model inference.
contributions: LPDDR5X-based CXL memory architecture achieving 16× capacity and 10× bandwidth improvements over GDDR6/DDR5 alternatives
CXL-PNM controller architecture integrated with LLM inference accelerator
Software stack enabling seamless transparent CXL-PNM use in Python-based LLM applications
Demonstration of 23% latency reduction, 31% throughput improvement, and 2.8× energy efficiency at 30% lower cost versus 8-GPU systems
